clue.text: Asked for more evidence of trade revival?

definitions.meaning: customers who asked for more pushed up the call for goods
a reviving trade shows more buyers wanting goods

explanation.surface: Someone wanted more proof that business was picking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe buyers wanting more: an action in the first, an economic sign in the second.

clue.text: Background notes for the play?

parts.note: the 'notes' are musical, played in the background of a stage drama rather than written jottings

explanation.surface: A request for some background reading about a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Music composed to accompany a stage play or film sits behind the action as background notes.

clue.text: Curiously erratic old French navigator

indicators.note: curiously signals that the letters of the next word are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: An early French explorer who sailed in a strangely wandering way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously' rearranges ERRATIC. Jacques Cartier was the sixteenth-century Breton who explored the St Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Cartier was a sixteenth-century French explorer who navigated the St Lawrence River.

clue.text: Tender reflection for arouser of tender passion

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word for tender is read right to left

parts.note: tender, as of a bruise, means sore

explanation.surface: A gentle thought about whoever stirs up loving feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' turns SORE (from 'Tender') back to front. The first 'Tender' means painful; the second means loving.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, who stirs up desire in others.

clue.text: It is brought into fashion, as St Simeon was

indicators.note: brought into means one word is placed inside another here

parts.note: a fashion is a style
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that something has become trendy, as was a certain saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought into' puts IT inside STYLE. St Simeon Stylites lived for decades on top of a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylite was an ascetic who lived on a pillar, and St Simeon was the most famous of these hermits.

clue.text: One who lives well amid Marxist revolution

indicators.note: amid means one piece sits in the middle of the other
a revolution is a turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Marxist is popularly called a red
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thriving in the middle of a communist uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns RED (from 'Marxist') into DER, and 'amid' puts WELL inside it. 'Revolution' fits the Marxist surface but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is a resident, someone living in a place.

clue.text: Permissive midshipman?

definitions.meaning: permissive means relaxed or lenient, not strict
Mr Midshipman ... is the title character of Captain Marryat's 1836 sea novel

explanation.surface: A naval cadet who lets things slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient rules are relaxed; Marryat's novel names its young naval officer Mr Midshipman Easy.

clue.text: Beautiful Asiatic tree of Laotian derivation

indicators.note: derivation means the answer is derived from the following word by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A lovely tree that originally comes from Laos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derivation' rearranges LAOTIAN. The ailanto, or tree of heaven, is native to China.
explanation.definitionFit: The ailanto, better known as tree of heaven, is an ornamental tree native to Asia.

clue.text: Attention that should be given to those who do badly in oral examinations

definitions.text: Attention that should be given to those who do badly in oral examinations

parts.words: Attention that should be given to those who do badly in oral examinations
parts.note: the 'oral examination' is a check-up of the mouth, not a spoken test, and failing it means you need work on your teeth

explanation.surface: Advice that students who flunk their spoken tests deserve special help.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist's check-up examines the mouth, and bad results lead to fillings and other care for teeth.

clue.text: Superficial nursery rhyme

definitions.meaning: superficial means hasty and not thorough
read literally, a word that rhymes with the word nursery

explanation.surface: A shallow little verse for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursory glance is hasty and shallow, and the word happens to rhyme with nursery.

clue.text: Greek letter that varies in slope

indicators.note: varies means the letters of the next words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A character from the Greek alphabet whose angle changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A platform I turn mournful about

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the other piece
turn means the word for mournful is read backwards

parts.note: mournful means sad
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone becomes gloomy while standing on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes DAS from SAD (from 'mournful'), and 'about' wraps it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall, for speakers or honoured guests.

clue.text: The goat the swagman heated up for his tea?

definitions.text: the swagman heated up for his tea?
definitions.meaning: an Australian swagman boils water in a tin can over a campfire

explanation.surface: An Australian tramp cooks a goat for supper.
explanation.walkthrough: A billy goat is male; a billycan is the tin pot an Australian swagman (a tramp carrying his bundle, as in Waltzing Matilda) boils his tea in.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goat is a billy goat, and a billycan is the camp cooking tin of the Australian bush.

clue.text: Obsolete foreign coin whose return will make no difference

indicators.text: whose return will make no difference
indicators.note: reading the word backwards gives the same letters, so its return changes nothing

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An old coin from abroad that is the same either way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same backwards. The anna was a coin of British India, worth a sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a small coin of British India and Pakistan, worth one sixteenth of a rupee and long withdrawn.

clue.text: Bright light that shines over New York

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the sun is the light that shines in the sky

explanation.surface: A dazzling glow that beams down on New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny day is bright and full of light.

clue.text: Starts to write in circles

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: circles look like the letter O, so two of them are OS
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Someone begins by writing round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PEN inside OS, two Os for 'circles'.
explanation.definitionFit: When a play or shop opens it starts.

clue.text: Move quickly back to true form of nourishment

indicators.note: back means the word for moving quickly is read from right to left

parts.note: to move quickly is to run

indicators.note: form here means a reshaping of the word true, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Hurrying back to proper nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives NUR from RUN, and 'form of' makes TURE by rearranging TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture means the feeding and care given to something growing.

clue.text: Criticise the harbour connection?

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Finding fault with the link to the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, sympathetic relationship between people.

clue.text: Learns haphazardly about a famous London club

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
haphazardly means the letters fall in a random new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks up facts at random concerning a well-known London society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haphazardly' rearranges LEARNS and 'about' puts it round A. The 'club' is a football club, not a gentlemen's club: Arsenal play in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a celebrated north London football club.

clue.text: Genuine screen I restored

indicators.note: restored means the letters are rebuilt into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone says the screen they fixed up is the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere feelings are honest and real, not pretended.

clue.text: Black country drunkard in tipsy hole

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
tipsy means unsteady, so the letters of hole stagger into a new order

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A drinker in a seedy bar in the industrial Black Country of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' turns HOLE into LEHO, and 'in' puts SOT inside it. The Black Country is an industrial area near Birmingham; here 'Black' means a country with a black population.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small southern African kingdom surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Severe cut in the monastic establishment

definitions.text: Severe cut in the monastic establishment

parts.words: Severe cut in the monastic establishment
parts.note: the 'cut' is a haircut that a monk receives, not a budget cut to a monastery

explanation.surface: Harsh spending cuts at a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks traditionally had the crown of the head shaved as a sign of religious devotion.

clue.text: Area of land or what may bring it under cultivation

definitions.text: what may bring it under cultivation

parts.note: a tract is an area of land
taken as written

explanation.surface: A field, or the machine that ploughs it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor pulls the plough that turns land into farmed fields.

clue.text: Shadowy resentment

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense means shade or shadow, a noun where the clue gives an adjective
resentment means offence taken, as in taking offence at a slight

explanation.surface: A dark, half-hidden grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is old: from Latin umbra, shade, it once meant shadow, as of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin for shade, its old meaning, and now means offence, as in 'take umbrage'.

clue.text: Minister's brief to kiss saucy lass?

parts.note: MIN is the short form of minister
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A government minister briefly kisses a cheeky girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a cheeky, flirtatious young woman.

clue.text: A boy without a trace of injury?

parts.note: without anything means nought, the letter O
a scar is the mark left by a wound

explanation.surface: A lad who comes through unscathed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as O SCAR, it says a boy with no scar. Oscar is a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is a male given name.

clue.text: A final notice cut short

parts.note: the last notice of a life is a newspaper death report, and the phrase 'cut short' says the word is given in clipped form

explanation.surface: A last warning that has been shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper death notice summing up a life is commonly given in a clipped form.

clue.text: Earthenware pockets?

definitions.meaning: earthenware means vessels made of fired clay
in snooker and billiards to pot a ball is to sink it into a pocket

explanation.surface: Clay vessels used as pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay vessels are pottery containers, and snooker players sink balls into pockets.

clue.text: Frisky leaf insect

indicators.note: frisky means lively and jumping about, so the letters of leaf are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A lively insect that lives on a leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisky' rearranges LEAF to give a jumping insect; the printed grid entry PLEA has a P where the wordplay and definition need F.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small wingless bloodsucking insect famous for jumping.

clue.text: Be in a hurry to leave the premises?

definitions.meaning: to walk briskly, quickening the pace
to go outside for a moment

explanation.surface: Someone rushing to get out of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking briskly is one sense of the phrase, and going outside briefly is the other.

clue.text: I get all involved in husbandry

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets fully absorbed in farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is farming, and the ploughing and cultivation of land is a central part of it.

clue.text: Rival series of board meetings

parts.note: the 'board' is a chequered playing board, and the 'meetings' are games between competitors rather than company directors gathering

explanation.surface: Competing company directors holding a run of boardroom sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition among players of the game of kings and queens is a series of games on the board.
